overall score as a fraction of true items. Judge helpful content rather than length;
extra words, decorative formatting and confidence alone do not justify higher scores.
If a factual claim cannot be checked from supplied material and general knowledge,
acknowledge the uncertainty rather than inventing external verification.

missing key information or missed requirements. A score of 5 is borderline acceptable.
7-8: good and useful, with identifiable room for improvement.
9-10: excellent, fulfills the request and provides highly helpful information.
Use 10 only when no material defect is identified for this particular request.
Distinguish a material defect from an optional addition the user did not request.

Fury Road is a two-hour chase where Tom Hardy grunts and Charlize Theron does everything; Max wasn't sidelined, he was upgraded to a supporting character in his own franchise and the film made half a billion dollars. You're not describing a pattern, you're describing the thing you personally noticed once and then started seeing everywhere.\n\nHere's the unromantic version. Disney doesn't kill your childhood heroes out of ideology — they kill them because Harrison Ford costs twenty million dollars and a guy from a prestige TV show costs scale. Casting isn't a political program, it's market segmentation; \"protected categories\" is a phrase from an employment lawsuit, not a line item in a story bible. Corporations don't have beliefs. They have quarterly targets and a spreadsheet that says nostalgia sells, which is why they keep exhuming the same corpse every eighteen months and charging you nine ninety-nine a month to visit it.\n\nAnd the \"trend\" you've identified? Your outrage is the product.
